meta.title: Smart TV, IP Camera, PC/Workstation & Network Device Security Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Performs non-intrusive discovery and security auditing across Smart TVs (Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku ECP, Google TV / Android TV / Chromecast, Sony Bravia, Vizio SmartCast, Philips JointSpace, Apple AirPlay, DIAL), IP Cameras / NVRs (RTSP 554/8554, ONVIF SOAP, Hikvision ISAPI, Dahua, Axis, Xiongmai, UniFi Protect, unauthenticated snapshots), PCs / Workstations / Local Servers (Windows SMB/NetBIOS/MSRPC/RDP/WinRM/WSDAPI, macOS/Linux SSH/VNC/CUPS/NFS/AFP/rsync/mDNS, Docker TCP 2375, Ollama 11434, local dev servers, open shares), routers, printers, NAS, and IoT appliances.
meta.whyItMatters: Local network devices and workstations often expose unauthenticated REST/WebSocket control APIs, live RTSP/MJPEG camera feeds, cleartext admin UIs, unauthenticated Docker/Ollama/dev servers, or remote file-sharing and shell services (SMB 445, RDP 3389, WinRM 5985, ADB 5555, Telnet 23) that allow LAN attackers to hijack screens, view surveillance feeds, access files, or execute arbitrary commands.
meta.defaultFix: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.
meta.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.

groupedFindings.fix: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.
groupedFindings.title: Smart TV, IP Camera, PC/Workstation & Network Device Security Exposure
groupedFindings.remediation: Segment Smart TVs, IP cameras/NVRs, and IoT appliances onto isolated VLANs with client isolation enabled. Require authentication and HTTPS/TLS on camera and appliance admin interfaces, enforce RTSP Digest auth, disable unused UPnP/DLNA/ADB/Telnet services, bind local dev servers, Docker, and Ollama to 127.0.0.1, and restrict SMB/RDP/WinRM/SSH/VNC/NFS via host firewalls.

groupedFindings.name: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
groupedFindings.detail: Target HTTP transport routed via Source IP 104.21.43.139 (104.21.43.139:80); no origin WAF bypass or default vhost leakage detected.

meta.title: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies whether the target connects via a resolved or configured Source/Origin IP and checks if direct Source-IP HTTP/HTTPS requests bypass CDN/WAF edge protections or leak internal default virtual-host / origin server metadata.
meta.whyItMatters: When an origin server accepts direct HTTP/HTTPS connections on its Source IP outside the CDN/WAF IP allowlist, attackers can bypass edge WAF rules, rate limits, and bot protections by connecting directly to the Source IP.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).
meta.remediation: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

groupedFindings.fix: Restrict origin firewall / security-group ingress on ports 80 and 443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a strict default-deny catch-all virtual host that rejects unknown Host headers or direct-IP TLS handshakes (nginx ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).
groupedFindings.title: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
groupedFindings.remediation: Restrict origin firewall / security-group ingress on ports 80 and 443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a strict default-deny catch-all virtual host that rejects unknown Host headers or direct-IP TLS handshakes (nginx ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

findings.name: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
findings.detail: Target HTTP transport routed via Source IP 104.21.43.139 (104.21.43.139:80); no origin WAF bypass or default vhost leakage detected.

meta.title: Direct Source-IP / Origin-IP HTTP Exposure & CDN/WAF Bypass
meta.plainExplanation: Verifies whether the target connects via a resolved or configured Source/Origin IP and checks if direct Source-IP HTTP/HTTPS requests bypass CDN/WAF edge protections or leak internal default virtual-host / origin server metadata.
meta.whyItMatters: When an origin server accepts direct HTTP/HTTPS connections on its Source IP outside the CDN/WAF IP allowlist, attackers can bypass edge WAF rules, rate limits, and bot protections by connecting directly to the Source IP.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).
meta.remediation: Restrict origin firewall ingress on ports 80/443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a default-deny catch-all virtual host (ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

findings.fix: Restrict origin firewall / security-group ingress on ports 80 and 443 to trusted CDN/WAF IP ranges only, configure a strict default-deny catch-all virtual host that rejects unknown Host headers or direct-IP TLS handshakes (nginx ssl_reject_handshake on; return 444;), and enforce Authenticated Origin Pulls (mTLS).

meta.title: System & Operational Health Exposure
meta.plainExplanation: Scans for exposed operational telemetry (/metrics, /prometheus, /server-status, /actuator/health), server 5xx errors, slow response latency, uncompressed payloads, and expiring TLS certificates.
meta.whyItMatters: Publicly accessible operational metrics, server status, and detailed component health dumps reveal internal architectures, infrastructure utilization, and sensitive service names to unauthorized actors.
meta.defaultFix: Restrict operational and telemetry endpoints to authorized monitoring networks or require authentication. Enable gzip/brotli compression, resolve backend server errors, and renew SSL/TLS certificates before expiration.
